A.explanation: A wavelength of $10^{-9} \text{ m}$ is in the X-ray region, not gamma ray, as gamma rays have much shorter wavelengths below about $10^{-11} \text{ m}$.

B.explanation: A wavelength of $10^{-5} \text{ m}$ is in the infrared region, as microwaves have much longer wavelengths of about $10^{-3} \text{ m}$ to $10^{-1} \text{ m}$.

C.explanation: A wavelength of $10^{-8} \text{ m}$ lies in the ultraviolet range of about $4 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$ to $10^{-8} \text{ m}$, just shorter than visible light.

D.explanation: A wavelength of $10^{-14} \text{ m}$ is in the gamma ray region, as X-rays have longer wavelengths of about $10^{-8} \text{ m}$ to $10^{-12} \text{ m}$.

hints: Recall the order of the electromagnetic spectrum from longest wavelength to shortest wavelength and place gamma ray, X-ray, ultraviolet, visible, infrared and microwave in that order.

Remember typical boundary values in $\text{m}$: gamma rays below $10^{-11} \text{ m}$, X-rays $10^{-8} \text{ m}$ to $10^{-12} \text{ m}$, ultraviolet $10^{-7} \text{ m}$ to $10^{-8} \text{ m}$, infrared $10^{-3} \text{ m}$ to $10^{-6} \text{ m}$.
Compare each given power of ten $10^{-9}$, $10^{-5}$, $10^{-8}$ and $10^{-14}$ against those ranges to see which pairing matches and which are one or more regions away.
walkthrough: List the spectrum in order of decreasing wavelength: radio, microwave, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-ray, gamma ray, so wavelength decreases from about $10^{4} \text{ m}$ to $10^{-16} \text{ m}$.

Recall approximate ranges: microwaves $10^{-1} \text{ m}$ to $10^{-3} \text{ m}$, infrared $10^{-3} \text{ m}$ to $7 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$, ultraviolet $4 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$ to $10^{-8} \text{ m}$, X-rays $10^{-8} \text{ m}$ to $10^{-12} \text{ m}$, gamma rays shorter than about $10^{-11} \text{ m}$.
Check $10^{-9} \text{ m}$ against gamma ray: it is about 100 to 1000 times too long and falls in the X-ray band, so that pairing is wrong.
Check $10^{-5} \text{ m}$ against microwave: it is about 100 times too short and falls in the infrared band, so that pairing is wrong.
Check $10^{-14} \text{ m}$ against X-ray: it is about 100 to 1000 times too short and falls in the gamma ray band, so that pairing is wrong.

Check $10^{-8} \text{ m}$ against ultraviolet: $10^{-8} \text{ m}$ equals $10 \text{ nm}$, which is at the short-wavelength end of the ultraviolet band just beyond visible light and X-rays. This is option C.
